design_summary.purpose: Parameterized PWM controller that generates a programmable pulse-width-modulated output from an 8-bit counter, with synchronous active-low reset and enable-controlled counting.
design_summary.operating_model: On each rising edge of clk, the internal counter state is cleared to zero when reset_n is low, held when enable is low, and otherwise incremented with inclusive terminal-count rollover at period. pwm_out is a purely combinational compare of counter_value against duty_cycle and counter_value is made externally observable as an output. The design is single-clock, single-reset, and uses no internal memory macros.

external_interfaces.name: clk
external_interfaces.role: Primary clock for all sequential behavior.

external_interfaces.name: reset_n
external_interfaces.role: Synchronous active-low reset for register state.

external_interfaces.name: enable
external_interfaces.role: Controls whether the counter advances or holds.

external_interfaces.name: duty_cycle
external_interfaces.role: Programmable PWM threshold used by the combinational compare.

external_interfaces.name: period
external_interfaces.role: Inclusive terminal count used for counter rollover.

external_interfaces.name: pwm_out
external_interfaces.role: Combinational PWM output asserted when counter_value is less than duty_cycle.

module_architecture.name: pwm_controller
module_architecture.role: Single-module top-level implementation of the PWM generator.
responsibilities: Generate a periodic count sequence under enable control.
Provide a duty-cycle-based PWM output derived from the current count.
Support synchronous active-low reset of all registers to zero.
Expose the current counter value as an output for monitoring and system use.
interface_notes: Consumes clk, reset_n, enable, duty_cycle, and period only; these are not driven internally.
Drives pwm_out and counter_value only; no other outputs or sideband signals are defined.
counter_value reflects the registered state directly and is the basis for rollover and external observability.
pwm_out is derived combinationally from counter_value and duty_cycle and is not separately registered.
ownership_notes: Owns the internal 8-bit counter register state.
Owns the enable-controlled increment and terminal-count rollover policy.
Owns reset clearing behavior for all internal registers.
Owns the public timing-visible PWM compare behavior through combinational output logic.

data_flow_summary.description: The clock and reset jointly govern synchronous state transitions, while enable qualifies whether the counter holds or advances.
The PWM output is a direct combinational compare: pwm_out is high when counter_value is numerically less than duty_cycle.
The current registered count is compared against period to determine whether the next counted state loads zero or increments.
The registered count state is exported unchanged for monitoring and downstream use.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single clock domain on clk at the specified 50.0 MHz nominal frequency / 20.0 ns period.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: reset_n is synchronous and active-low. When reset_n is low, the counter register is cleared to 8'h00 on the next rising edge of clk, which forces counter_value to zero. Because pwm_out is a combinational compare of counter_value and duty_cycle, it follows the cleared state immediately after the registered update. No other state elements are implied.

integration_notes: period is treated as an inclusive terminal count for rollover: when enable is high and the current counter_value equals period, the next state becomes zero.
duty_cycle and period are sampled combinationally for the compare and rollover decision, respectively.
The design has no memory macros and no hidden state beyond the counter register implied by the functionality.
The module is fully self-contained and intended for direct integration at the top level using the inherited port list and rtl_output_file pwm_controller.v.
